extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (Korean patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for determining inventive step (obviousness) and the enlarged concept of novelty under the Korean Patent Act, including how to treat combination inventions, prior applications under Article 29, and relevant secondary evidence. Intended to guide examination and applicant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-characterizable manufacturing-method claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claimed invention (e.g., a product defined by a manufacturing method) can be characterized by certain properties, features, and composition based on the method description, the examiner can determine inventive step by comparing the product defined by the manufacturing method with the cited invention without considering the manufacturing method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a belt coupling apparatus described with a manufacturing method — if there is no difficulty characterizing the seat belt via its composition, inventive step may be determined by comparing the product with prior art, disregarding the manufacturing steps. Conversely, if the manufacturing method produces a measurable change in product properties (e.g., increased inorganic content in tea leaves by heating/IR), inventive step may be acknowledged because of the change in product properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of combination invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A combination invention comprises novel solutions by gathering technical features disclosed in the prior art as a whole in order to solve a technical problem. The invention described in a claim is to be considered as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of inventive step for combination inventions relies on the technical idea of the claimed invention as a whole, not on whether each individual element is known. Examiner shall consider difficulty in forming structurally combined elements and the unique effect the invention has as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining multiple prior-art disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining inventive step by combining more than two disclosures is allowed, but limited to situations where a person skilled in the art could easily combine the disclosures at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No strict limit on the number of prior-art disclosures to be combined, but when combining various prior arts, the examiner mainly considers whether the cited inventions contain a motivation or hint leading to the claimed invention by combining the disclosures, the state of the art, common general knowledge, technical trends and industry demands. If combination is deemed easily made by a skilled person, inventive step may be denied (citing relevant precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-known art vs commonly-used art
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-known art: technologies generally known in the relevant technical field (widely known throughout the industry or appearing in many prior-art disclosures). Commonly-used art: well-known art which is used widely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when assessing whether a prior-art element is so routine that combining it with other disclosures would be obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of motivation/hint for combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a prior-art disclosure contains a motivation, hint, or the like for a combination shall be made by synthetically assessing whether the motivation/hint is explicitly taught in prior art, inherent from the technical problem, or part of common general knowledge/empirical rules of a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate evaluating explicit teaching (citation referring to another disclosure), inherent suggestion from the problem to be solved, or whether the hint is within the common general knowledge (e.g., public reports leading a skilled person to substitute materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art references to other disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior-art disclosure that refers to another disclosure can be considered to explicitly suggest a hint or motivation for a combination, and it is regarded as obvious to combine the two disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining a plurality of technical features disclosed in the same document is also considered obvious because a person skilled in the art would combine them without difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining well-known technology with other prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: It is normally considered obvious to combine a well-known technology with another prior-art disclosure; however, if the combination results in an advantageous effect, the combination may not be regarded as obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if one cited invention lacks a leading portion and that portion is substantially the same as a guide member in another cited invention referred to therein, the combination may be considered implied and obvious — unless an advantageous unexpected effect arises from the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergistic effect / functional interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If a combination invention achieves an effect by functional interaction between technical features that is different from or greater than the sum of effects of the individual features (a combined synergistic effect), the inventive step may be acknowledged because the set of features is a technically meaningful combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the combination is merely a juxtaposition/aggregation (simple collection) without particular difficulties or remarkable functional difference, the invention is likely to be denied inventive step. Examples contrast meaningful synergistic combinations vs aggregations (e.g., ordinary injection molding + vacuum chamber + mold fastening system producing no remarkable difference => aggregation => obvious).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of how many prior arts are combined
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken because the higher number of combined cited inventions, the more likely the claimed invention results from an ex post facto view or lacks a valid reason for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining whether it would have been obvious to combine two or more prior arts, examiner should consider: (①) whether there is a good possibility to combine them, ②) whether the prior arts come from similar or neighboring technical fields, and ③) whether there is a reasonable basis to associate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other non-structural factors as secondary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond technical constitution and functional effect, other factors may be taken into account as secondary evidence when an applicant submits written opinions asserting non-obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such factors include: (1) prior art teaching away (a prior document that precludes reasoning leading to the invention), (2) commercial success or favorable industry comments (indicative only if success derives from technical features), (3) solving long-felt needs or problems attempts, (4) use of technical means abandoned due to technical prejudice, (5) overcoming technical difficulties not resolvable by other means, and (6) being in a brand-new technology area with no relevant prior art. These are generally supporting evidence; they do not replace analysis of the specification's disclosed contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution against ex post facto reasoning from the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining inventive step in light of knowledge obtained from matters disclosed in the specification under examination, examiners should avoid concluding obviousness by using the specification (i.e., avoid ex post facto analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if cited invention merely mentions an objective like 'preventing others noticing a voice reception' but does not disclose the specific technical structure (e.g., tapping mode blocking reception while allowing emission), it is improper to conclude obviousness by retrofitting the claimed structure to the cited disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim has an inventive step, a claim dependent on that independent claim is deemed to have an inventive step too. If the independent claim does not have an inventive step, determination should be made for each dependent claim individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When independent claim lacks inventive step, do not automatically dismiss dependents — examine their specific limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product inventions imply process/use inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: If a product invention explicitly has an inventive step, a process invention for making the product or a use invention for using the product also has an inventive step in principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general presumption; specific process/use claims still need individual assessment when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush/multiple-selective alternatives caution
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims in Markush form or comprising multiple selective technical features, if at least one Markush alternative is proven not to have an inventive step based on prior art, the applicant can be notified of refusal for the claim; the applicant may overcome refusal by deleting alternatives that lack inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care must be taken not to expand the effect of one selective element to the whole claimed invention. All alternatives (e.g., chemical compounds) must show remarkable effect over cited prior inventions for grant based on that effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degenerate inventions lack inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: A degenerate invention does not involve an inventive step and granting a patent on a degenerate invention runs against the purpose of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degenerate inventions are barely conducted and may have negative effects on users; examiners should refuse such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidential requirements for asserting well-known technology
rubrics_metrics.description: If the cited invention is regarded as a well-known technology, the examiner may notify the applicant of refusal without attaching evidential material; however, it is inappropriate to regard a technology as the closest cited invention without evidential material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant disputes that technology is well-known in a written opinion, examiner should in principle provide evidential material (e.g., textbooks, standards) or fully explain why the invention falls under well-known technology and why the applicant's argument is not proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign examination precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step is individually determined and examination precedents in foreign countries that differ in legal systems and customs are not taken into consideration for a specific patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on foreign case law as determinative in domestic inventive-step assessments when legal frameworks differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal prohibition irrelevant to inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation prohibited by law (domestic or foreign) is not taken into consideration in determining inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if claimed method is illegal (e.g., certain lottery drawing methods), inventive step is assessed on technical difficulty and not on legal permissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 29(3)/(4) — earlier application as prior art (enlarged novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention claimed in a patent application is identical with an invention described in the specification or drawings originally attached to another application filed prior to the filing date of the concerned application and later laid open/published, the patent may not be granted — with exceptions where inventors/applicants are the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: prevent giving exclusive rights to later applicants for inventions already contributed to the public via earlier laid-open specifications/drawings. The proviso allows exceptions if inventor or applicant is the same person at time of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for applying Article 29(3)/(4): filing-date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Another application cited under Article 29(3)/(4) must have a filing date prior to the filing date of the present application. For divisional/converted applications, the actual filing date of the divisional/converted application is the critical date (not the original application date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if filing date of the divisional is after present application filing date, the divisional cannot be cited, but the original application may be cited if its filing date is prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim effects for determining filing date of another application
rubrics_metrics.description: If another application is one with a priority claim under the Paris Convention, the filing date in the country of origin is deemed the filing date for inventions commonly disclosed in the original specification/drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only inventions actually disclosed in the priority-country filing count for the earlier filing date; inventions missing from that filing cannot be cited under Article 29(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of commonly disclosed matters between prior and subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner cites an invention initially disclosed in the specification of a prior application that was a basis for a domestic priority claim or a subsequent application, matters commonly disclosed in initial specifications of both prior and subsequent applications are treated as having filing date of the prior application (or sometimes the subsequent application depending on domestic priority rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules distinguish inventions commonly disclosed in both, inventions solely in initial specification of subsequent (treated as filed on subsequent filing date), and inventions solely disclosed in initial specification of prior (not applied). Amended disclosures after filing are not treated as laid-open for Article 29(3)/(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that the claimed invention be identical to invention in initial specification of another application
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention described in the claims of the present application should be completely or substantially identical to an invention or device described in the initial specification of another application to trigger Article 29(3)/(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the matters were omitted by amendment after filing, Article 29(3) still applies. The 'identity' requirement is substantive (complete or substantial identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laid-open/publication requirement for another application
rubrics_metrics.description: Another application must have been laid open or published for registration after the present application was filed; once laid open/published, the application remains effective as another application despite later refusal, invalidation, withdrawal, or abandonment (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior application was laid open and then refused or invalidated, it may still serve as another application; but if laid open after decision of refusal/invalidation/withdrawal/abandonment, it may not be cited under Article 29(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisos excluding prior application under Article 29(3)/(4): same inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is not considered 'another application' under Article 29(3)/(4) where the inventor of the present application is the same as the inventor of the other application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor identity is judged from the inventor described in application documents; in joint inventions, all inventors must be identical. If discrepancies exist, applicant may prove practical identity; amendments to inventorship after refusal allow applicants to request documentary proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisos excluding prior application under Article 29(3)/(4): same applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is not considered 'another application' under Article 29(3)/(4) where the applicant of the present application at time of filing is the same as the applicant of the other application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant identity is compared at time of filing; for plural applicants all must match. Subsequent changes (name change, inheritance, merger) do not negate substantial sameness if applicants are substantially the same at filing.
